Coming from the perspective of a software developer, this may be asking for a lot more than you may think. It's one thing to keep track of an integer, incrementing it whenever you upvoat something and decrementing it whenever you nullify an upvoat (which is how I assume it works right now).

It's another thing entirely to keep track of which comments or posts a user has upvoated and maintaining that for every user on the site. In my opinion this would require a much larger memory overhead and could potentially result in worse performance of the site overall, since every time an upvoat is added/removed it would require a call to the server to update the user's upvoat tracker.

What's more is that once a user has been using Voat for some time, the number of upvoated items will grow incredibly large but will be accessed relatively infrequently, especially upvoated items from some time ago. One solution to that issue would be to stop keeping track of upvoats past a certain date, but the implementation would likely still incur the above downsides.

There's also the question of what to do with upvoated items of users who are no longer active. If the above solution were used (removing anything older than a certain date), this would not be an issue. Otherwise there would have to be some thought put into when a user should be considered inactive or abandoned and if their upvoated items list should be purged.

I don't mean to be a Debbie Downer, but the ratio between how much functionality is added and how many resources are spent implementing/maintaining this feature seems to be too imbalanced for it to be likely that this is feasible. Just my two cents.
